title: Mathematical discoveries from program search with large language models

mechanism.domainTask: LLM-guided executable program search for mathematical and combinatorial discovery
mechanism.populationDetail: Correct programs are held in m persistent islands; each island evolves separately and participates in periodic cross-island reseeding.
mechanism.archiveDetail: No separate elite archive is described; signature clusters organize the island populations and are not reported as one-elite-per-cell archive storage.
mechanism.replacementDetail: Correct programs are incrementally inserted into their source island, while every four hours the lowest-scoring half of islands are cleared and each is reseeded from a highest-scoring program in a uniformly chosen surviving island.
mechanism.generationDetail: The prompt samples two programs from one island and explicitly aims for the LLM to merge their ideas while completing the critical function in a fixed program skeleton.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: Per-input score signatures form clusters and aggregate cluster scores drive Boltzmann sampling; invalid or resource-failing programs are not stored.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: First choose an island uniformly, then choose a score-biased signature cluster, then a shorter-program-biased member; the selected two programs are used jointly.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: Within-island score-signature clustering with score-biased cluster sampling and shorter-program preference combines diversity-aware selection with island-level periodic reset/reseeding.

provenance.citationWarning: Do not equate within-island score-signature clustering with a separate quality-diversity elite archive: the paper describes clustered population storage but does not specify one elite per niche. Replacement mixes incremental insertion with periodic island reset/reseed. Exploration is explicitly motivated but lacks an explicit E/E controller.
